newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar immobile in Tokyo ahead of U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: Dollar immobile in Tokyo ahead of U.S. holiday.

text.p: The dollar virtually stalled against the yen and mark throughout Thursday trade, sandwiched between effects of the Bank of Japan tankan report on Wednesday and ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday later, dealers said.
With a lack of fresh factors and energy, the dollar failed to move out of a tight 113.12-40 yen cage in which Japanese investors were placing bids at the lower side of the range.
"With major events such as the BOJ's tankan behind us, the market here was dead quiet," said a Japanese bank dealer.

Dealers said sporadic selling interest from Japanese exporters and overseas funds was detected at 113.40 yen, while Japanese investors were keen to pick up dollars at 113.00 yen and below related to their fresh investment in foreign assets.

They said they did not see any big moves in the near future but were generally expecting the dollar to head higher towards the end of the year. Profit transfers of American firms' subsidiaries in Japan and Japanese individual investors' demand for foreign bonds were behind their bullish view on the dollar.
"There may be a chance that the dollar will re-test 115 yen by the year-end," said a dealer at a European bank.

The dollar rose as high as 114.92 yen in late October before declining to the 110 yen level on remarks in early November by a senior Japanese Finance Ministry official signalling discomfort about the yen's sharp falls. "The focus will be on whether the official will talk down the dollar. Trading may become a bit nervous when the dollar goes up above 113.50 yen," he added. Longer-term, fears of a rising trend in Japan's trade surplus with the U.S., which will likely be more marked next year, may be a dollar-selling factor.
Thursday's announcement that Japan's industrial production rose a preliminary 3.5 percent in October from September, seasonally adjusted, was in line with market expectations.
But the future outlook was less optimistic, with the trade ministry forecasting a fall of 1.7 percent for November.
Japanese government bonds gained slightly on the report, but the currency market was little moved by it.

In cross trade, the yen remained weak, with the British pound outperforming others in recent tradings due to lingering expectations of a rise in British interest rates and of lack of credit tightening in Japan until late 1997, dealers said.
The pound rallied overnight and rose to the 190 yen level for the first time since early 1993. It stood at 190.20/32 at 0656 GMT against 190.03 yen in late New York on Wednesday.
Analysts say the British budget unveiled on Tuesday was not restrictive enough and rates should rise to quell nascent inflation.

Meanwhile, the Bank of Japan's tankan survey released on Wednesday strengthened views that Japan will stick to its current low interest rate policy, spurring buying of the pound for the yen by Japanese investors, dealers said.
